questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area of the Image of an Object Under a Linear Transformation
questions.problem:
The Unit square $D$ has vertices $(1,0),(0,0),(0,1),(1,1).$ What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064490/assets/6805467a24cb40559f205cbfcecc4f5a34ff2ec6ebda8ae67f997c02f123b53c.png)

Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=1\cdot 1=1.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
det(T)=4\cdot 2-3\cdot 2=2.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,2\,|\cdot 1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 7\cdot 4=14.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$

$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,7\,|\cdot 14 \\  & =98.\end{aligned}
